trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the market's implied probability move persists or was a thin-liquidity blip; compare to front-end rate futures (SOFR/Fed funds) for corroboration.
time_plan.1h: Watch 2s and 10s yields and TLT; confirm bonds are rallying rather than a data-driven equity/bond decoupling.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether any macro news (jobless claims, Fed speak, geopolitical shock) explains the shift and whether it is already public.
time_plan.6h: Evaluate whether the move is sustained into the US session and whether Fed funds futures have shifted dovishly.
time_plan.12h: Mark final TLT return vs prediction; note whether the anomaly led, lagged, or was noise relative to rate futures.

predictions.reasoning: A market on 12+ Fed cuts in 2026 (~300bps of easing) is a deep-dovish/crisis tail. A sharp rise in its implied probability would reflect expectations of aggressive Fed easing, which repriced into the curve pushes yields lower and long-duration bond prices up. TLT is the most direct, liquid proxy for a big downward shift in expected policy rates.

predictions.reasoning: Extreme expected Fed easing narrows US rate differentials, typically weakening the dollar. A jump in the probability of 12+ cuts implies a dovish repricing that pressures USD lower. However this is a weaker, noisier proxy: a crisis driving cut expectations can simultaneously spark safe-haven USD demand, muddying direction.

evidence_used: Market resolves on count of 25bp Fed cuts in 2026; 12+ cuts equals ~300bps of easing, an extreme dovish/emergency scenario
Description explicitly includes emergency inter-meeting cuts, signaling this is a crisis-tail question
Standard macro linkage: expected policy-rate cuts push bond yields down and pressure the dollar
uncertainty_notes: A 12+ cut scenario is a deep tail; probability changes may be tiny in absolute terms and dominated by thin liquidity/noise
Crisis-driven easing expectations can produce conflicting asset moves (bonds up but equities down and USD up as safe haven)
No headline confirms an actual policy shift; the market may simply be repricing speculatively
The mislabeled 'military_conflict' topic suggests possible metadata error, reducing confidence in interpretation

llm_justification.summary: This market on 12+ Fed cuts in 2026 encodes a deep-dovish/emergency-easing tail. A sharp rise in its implied probability would most cleanly map to lower expected policy rates: long Treasuries (TLT) rally and the dollar (UUP) tends to weaken. Both signals are noisy over a 12h window, magnitudes well below the 700bps tradable threshold, and confidence is modest because crisis dynamics can invert the FX leg and thin liquidity can distort the market reading.
key_assumptions: A move in this market reflects genuine dovish repricing rather than illiquid noise
Bond and FX markets react to shifting Fed-cut expectations in the conventional direction
No offsetting inflation-driven or safe-haven shock dominates within 12h
failure_modes: The prediction-market move reverses or was thin-liquidity noise with no real information
The easing expectation is already fully public and priced, so no residual asset move
TLT proxy is exposed to term premium/supply factors, not just policy-rate expectations
USD weakens vs strengthens ambiguity: a crisis triggering cut bets could drive safe-haven dollar buying, flipping the FX leg
Expected magnitudes are far below the 700bps tradable threshold, so neither is actionable
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
